(Today through Friday)...
Issued at 209 AM EDT Sat Sep 12 2026

An upper level wave will bring scattered showers and embedded 
thunderstorms this morning focused mainly across the southeast half 
of central Indiana. Additional isolated storms are possible this 
afternoon before weak high pressure builds in tonight. After a brief 
cooldown Monday...upper ridging will expand north into the region 
through the middle of next week with hot temperatures returning. A 
cold front will become nearly stationary across the lower Great 
Lakes before gradually sliding into the Ohio Valley during the 
second half of next week with increasing chances for showers and 
thunderstorms.

Today through Monday Night

Clouds were increasing from the southwest early this morning in 
response to an approaching upper level wave. Convection has been 
ongoing across the western Tennessee and lower Ohio Valleys since 
Friday evening and had now advanced into the lower Wabash Valley. 
06Z temperatures ranged from the mid 60s north to the mid 70s south.

The upper wave is the primary feature of interest in the near term 
as it pivots across the region through this afternoon. An organized 
area of convection will continue to track northeast across the 
forecast area through daybreak. While storms have had a history of 
stronger winds across far southwest Indiana...anticipate a gradual 
decrease in intensity as it lifts northeast through the forecast 
area with less instability present. The main concern from the storms 
will be the potential for locally heavy rainfall as PWATS near 2 
inches advect into the area and the airmass below 500mb is 
exceptionally moist. High rainfall rates have already been noted 
west of KEVV earlier and while a downtrend in convective intensity 
should lead to diminishing rates...there are likely to be some 
locations over the lower Wabash Valley and southern parts of the 
forecast area that see a quick 1 to 2 inches of rain.

The weakening area of convection will move east of the region during 
the first half of the morning with scattered lighter showers and an 
expansion of lower stratus enveloping much of the forecast area 
through midday. As the stratus mixes out into a cu field this 
afternoon and heating commences...potential is there for isolated 
convection developing across primarily the eastern half of the 
forecast area on the back side of the departing upper wave. MUCAPE 
levels increase to 1000-2000 j/kg with abundant moisture lingering. 
The convection will shift east by early evening as the upper wave 
moves away to the east.

Weak high pressure builds in tonight in the wake of the upper wave 
with cloud coverage diminishing. Could again see patchy fog near 
daybreak Sunday within the muggy airmass. Sunday will begin dry but 
the approach of a cold front from the northwest will spread the risk 
for scattered convection back into the forecast area for the 
afternoon and evening. A surge of cooler and much drier air will 
follow in the wake of the frontal passage Sunday night as a strong 
high pressure builds into the upper Midwest. The high will pivot 
across the Great Lakes on Monday with an axis of deep subsidence 
swinging across the area. Return southerly flow will begin to draw 
moisture back into the region as soon as Monday night with the high 
shifting into New England. The upper ridge will also progress 
towards the Ohio Valley setting the stage for a return to a hotter 
regime for Tuesday and Wednesday.

Temps...Highs today will range from around 80 in eastern parts of 
the forecast area where clouds and the threat for rain will last much 
of the day...to the mid 80s in the Wabash Valley. Low level thermals 
support highs in the low to mid 80s Sunday as well. With the Sunday 
night frontal passage...MOnday temperatures will pleasant ranging 
from the mid 70s in the northeast to the lower 80s in the Wabash 
Valley. 

Tuesday through Friday

Return southerly flow will develop on the back side of the departing 
high quickly on Tuesday as mid level heights rise across the Ohio 
Valley. Highs will likely warm back into the lower and possibly mid 
90s Tuesday and Wednesday as the upper ridge centers over the 
Tennessee Valley. With a frontal boundary stalled to the north over 
the Great Lakes...convective risks will be isolated and diurnally 
driven at best.

A retrogression of the ridge into the Southern Plains by late week 
will finally enable the front to press south into the region with an 
increasing threat for scattered convection across the forecast area. 
The heat will be pushed back south as well with temperatures sliding 
into the lower and mid 80s by Friday then into the upper 70s next 
weekend. Extended model guidance has backed off on the arrival of a 
much cooler airmass into the region perhaps not until the 10 to 14 
day range as a more chaotic quasi-zonal flow aloft remains across 
much of the northern half of the country by next weekend.
